title: Tutorials
text:
This section provides step-by-step tutorials to help you apply the Pathogen Genomics Competency Framework (PGCF) in practice.
Each tutorial is designed as a guided workflow. You can follow along from start to finish, using your own context (role, course, or organisation).

title: Getting Started
text:
The PGCF provides a structured way to understand, assess, and develop competencies required for pathogen genomics across laboratory science, bioinformatics, epidemiology, and public health.
Whether you are designing training, planning workforce development, or guiding your own learning, this section will help you get started quickly.

title: Getting Started
text:
The PGCF provides a structured way to understand, assess, and develop competencies required for pathogen genomics across laboratory science, bioinformatics, epidemiology, and public health.
Whether you are designing training, planning workforce development, or guiding your own learning, this section will help you get started quickly.

title: Getting Started
text:
2 What is a competency framework?
A competency framework defines the knowledge, skills, and attitudes (KSA) required to perform effectively in a specific domain.
In the context of pathogen genomics, this means: - Understanding laboratory and sequencing workflows
- Analysing and interpreting genomic data
- Applying insights in clinical and public health settings
- Working across disciplines and systems
The PGCF brings these elements together into a single, structured model.

title: Getting Started
text:
3 What makes PGCF different?
The PGCF is designed to reflect the full complexity of pathogen genomics in practice.

3.1 360° coverage
Covers the entire workflow: - Sample collection → sequencing → analysis → interpretation → decision-making


3.2 Role-spanning
Applies across: - Laboratory scientists
- Bioinformaticians
- Epidemiologists
- Clinicians
- Public health professionals


3.3 Structured progression (Bloom’s taxonomy)
Each competency is defined across six levels of complexity: - Remember → Understand → Apply → Analyse → Evaluate → Create


3.4 Knowledge, Skills, Attitudes (KSA)
Each competency is tagged to support: - Teaching design
- Assessment strategies
- Workforce planning

title: Getting Started
text:
4 When should you use PGCF?
Use the framework when you need to:

Design or improve a training programme

Map an existing course to competencies

Identify skills gaps in individuals or teams

Define role expectations

Support workforce planning

Guide your own professional development

title: Getting Started
text:
5 What does PGCF include?
The framework is part of a broader toolkit:

5.1 Framework structure

10 domains

60 topics

360 competency statements



5.2 Competency database

Searchable and structured

Organised by domain, topic, and Bloom’s level



5.3 Self-assessment tool

Identify required levels for your role

Generate a personalised competency profile



5.4 User guide and templates

Curriculum mapping

Gap analysis

Workforce planning tools

title: How-to Guides
text:
This section provides practical, task-focused guides to help you use the Pathogen Genomics Competency Framework (PGCF) to achieve specific goals.
Unlike tutorials, which walk you through a full workflow, these guides help you solve a particular problem or complete a defined task.

title: How-to Guides
section: 2 When should you use these guides?
text:
2 When should you use these guides?
Use the How-to Guides when you need to:

Perform a gap analysis
Map a curriculum or course
Define role profiles
Assess training needs
Integrate PGCF into an existing programme
Interpret competency levels in practice

If you are new to the framework, start with the Tutorials section first.

title: How-to Guides
text:
3 Available guides

3.1 🔍 Perform a gap analysis
Identify strengths and gaps in: - A curriculum
- A team or organisation
- A training programme
Use this to prioritise areas for development.



3.2 🧩 Map a curriculum to PGCF
Align your course or training programme with: - PGCF domains and topics
- Competency statements
- Expected levels of complexity



3.3 👥 Define role profiles
Create structured role definitions by: - Selecting relevant domains
- Assigning expected competency levels
- Clarifying responsibilities



3.4 📊 Conduct a training needs assessment
Use PGCF to: - Identify required competencies for a role or team
- Compare current vs expected levels
- Inform training plans



3.5 🎓 Integrate PGCF into short courses
Embed the framework into: - Course design
- Learning objectives
- Assessment strategies



3.6 🧠 Interpret Bloom’s levels in practice
Understand how to: - Translate levels into teaching and assessment
- Apply levels consistently across topics
- Avoid common misunderstandings



3.7 🌍 Use PGCF across sectors
Adapt the framework for: - Clinical settings
- Public health organisations
- Research environments

title: How-to Guides
text:
4 How to use these guides

title: template_course
text:
Course Overview
- Course Title
- Course Description: Short and extended versions
- Course format 
- Target Audience: (e.g., clinicians, researchers, students)
- Prerequisites: Knowledge or skills expected
 
Learning Outcomes
- Clearly defined, measurable outcomes using Blooms action verbs 
- Mapped to competencies if relevant
Assessment
- Formative assessments (quizzes, exercises, peer review)
- Summative assessments (final project, test, reflection)
- Rubrics and grading templates for instructors 
- Submission methods/platform
- Model answers or guides 
 
Teaching Platform & Tech Tools
- Platforms guide: e.g., GitHub Classroom, Google classroom, Moodle, Zoom etc 
- Accounts/Access setup instructions
- Tools used in communication and teaching: e.g., Zoom, Slack, BLAST, RStudio
- Instructions for setting up any required environments (Docker, Conda, virtual machines)
 
Resources & References
- Core readings (articles, textbooks)
- Supplementary materials (websites, tools, videos)
- Glossary of terms
- FAQs and Troubleshooting guide (tech and teaching)
 
Instructor & Facilitator Guide - important to include
- Adult learning strategies [see T3 resource] 
- Teaching tips for each module
- Common learner questions/issues 
- Discussion prompts
- Inclusivity guidance [see T3 resource, UDL] 
 
 
Evaluation & Feedback Templates
- Evaluation questions [what do we want to know] 
- Data collection: learner feedback forms, instructor reflection log/observation structured notes, ost course survey etc)
- Plan for data analysis 
- Plan for results dissemination
